text.p: The Turkish lira weakened to 89,830 per dollar from 89,670 at Monday's close, but firmed from an opening of 89,900 on early central bank intervention.

Bankers said the lira fell in the morning on dollar demand before the central bank stepped in to sell dollars to banks. It firmed to around 89,800 after the intervention, but again slipped lower in the afternoon due to a firmer dollar/mark parity.

The Turkish central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 89,625 lira at the opening after 89,550 at Monday's close, but later raised it to 89,675 due to the dollar's gains against the mark in world markets.

The central bank lent banks 42.2 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent due to a persistant cash squeeze. It had funded 40 trillion lira at the same rate on Monday. Overnight money rates also traded at 74.75 in the day.
The average overnight money rate firmed slightly to 74.95 from yesterday's 74.93.

The treasury sold 176.7 trillion lira worth of March 26, 1997 paper, meeting 68 percent of bids totalling 260.5 trillion lira at auction. It cut the average yield to 125.64 percent from 128.92 percent at the previous 182-day t-bill auction September 10.

The cash shortage is expected to continue on Wednesday when banks will cash in 79.6 trillion lira from the treasury for maturing t-bills. They will pay the treasury 114 trillion lira for today's auction and return 42.2 trillion lira of overnight borrowing to the central bank.
The central bank said it would open a five-day repo auction tomorrow to feed cash to the system.
T-bill yields eased mostly before the Treasury finalised its auction.
The yield on the most heavily traded February 12, 1997 paper dropped to 121.42 percent from an average of 122.36 percent on Monday.
The second most active March 12 paper yielded 124.76 percent, slightly up from yesterday's 124.72 percent.
March 26 paper sold at today's auction traded at 126.49 percent with Wednesday's value date after the auction. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
